The team achieved the primary goal of the project, which was to make significant strides developing zero-emission technologies for heavy-duty Class 8 trucks that would accelerate the improvement of air quality in southern California transportation corridors. This vehicle’s architecture blended existing zero-emission battery electric technology with a zero-emission hydrogen fuel cell engine acting as a range extender to create a zero-emission drayage truck. Project team members included the Center for Transportation and the Environment (CTE), Kenworth, BAE Systems, Ballard Power Systems, and Total Transport Solutions Inc. (TTSI). The project scope was split into two phases. During Phase I, the project team completed the design, build, test, and delivery of the prototype fuel cell hybrid electric drayage truck. The team also procured hydrogen and established a hydrogen fueling station for the use of all three SCAQMD drayage truck teams.
